evidence.curator_note: Substrate as drawn: a 2-alkanone molecular ion printed as C3H7-CH(H)-CH2-CH2-C(=O)-CH3 with the gamma hydrogen on C5 drawn EXPLICITLY and '+.' printed above the carbonyl oxygen. INSTANTIATION of the condensed 'C3H7' label (the page does not draw it out): it is taken as ISOPROPYL, making the compound 6-methyl-2-heptanone. That is not a guess -- the running text introducing this scheme rationalises 'the characteristic peaks in ... 6-methyl-2-heptanone (Figure 9.9)' and names 'a pair of acylium ions (m/z 113 and 43 in Figure 9.9) and a pair of alkyl ions (m/z 85 and 15)', which are exactly this equation's products. n-Propyl would give 2-octanone, an isomer with identical nominal masses at every step, so the drawing alone cannot distinguish them and the text is what settles it. LOCALIZATION (convention B): charge and odd electron are written on the oxygen where the page prints them, [C:2]=[O+:9]. Book draws 0 arc(s) on the molecular ion -- there is no fishhook anywhere on it; every arrow leaving it carries only a label. TOP channel: an arrow labelled 'alpha' rising to 'CH3CO+ / m/z 43'. Radical-site alpha cleavage of the C2-C3 bond with the charge retained on the ACETYL side. Book draws 0 arc(s), so all three moves are curator-supplied: the canonical triple <1> the oxygen odd electron into the forming C-O pi bond, <2> one electron of the breaking C2-C3 sigma bond into that same bond (raising C2-O9 from double to TRIPLE, the acylium the page writes as CH3CO+), <3> the other C2-C3 electron leaving with the hexyl radical. MS CONTEXT: the page prints no ionisation conditions, so 70 eV EI is the corpus house default, disclosed rather than read off the page. Figure 9.9 (printed p247) is the 6-methyl-2-heptanone spectrum and does carry abundances, but it is NOT this page and this scheme prints no percentage, so per convention F no relative_intensity is recorded; peaks are status 'proposed'.
